title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated detection being treated as an identification. A camera system flagged a vehicle as matching a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, but it could not read the plates. The unreadable alert was escalated anyway, to at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs. The failure sits at the handoff between a machine-generated alert and the human decision to act on it with force.

What would have caught it is the step that was skipped: confirming the plate before treating the car as the stolen one. The deputies themselves noted the plates were unreadable and called backup rather than resolving the ambiguity. A system that cannot read a plate has not established that the plate matches anything, and the stop proceeded as though it had.

It is not established that the deputy threatened to shoot, which is the men's account, and the sheriff's office review of body worn camera footage has not produced a finding. No charges were filed against the men, and the attorney has been described as planned rather than retained.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19 year old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and one deputy threatened to shoot, according to the men. Deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies after flock cameras picked up plates, but they could not read the plates and called backup. After handcuffing them, deputies realized it was the wrong car.

The men were released and not charged. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. The sheriff's office says supervisors will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. Both men were given information about filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
